proposedContributions.change: Define provider-neutral MailAccount/MailThread/MailMessage/MailLabel DTOs with Rox2EntityRef, revision, account namespace and provider aliases; immutable body references separate from mutable flags/labels. Publish strict mail.openThread account/thread validation and GetMailThread/QueryInbox pagination plus SendMail capability/result port. Reuse accepted RoxCommand v2/canonical result types and error mapping. Provider result includes email/submission IDs, actual capability and evidence provenance; queued/unknown never becomes verified because the adapter returned successfully. No credential values in DTOs.

Resolve authenticated actor before account and alias lookup; authorize source account separately from linked entity, constrain every lookup by workspace and account, bind cursors to actor/account/query/policy. Upsert canonical entities/aliases using shared registry in one transaction with revision/outbox receipt, persist immutable bodies and token references separately, and apply policy/tombstone fences before query serialization. Register exact HTTP/native RPC mail.openThread and common mail provider commands through existing authority. Persist outbound intent and provider evidence through the common receipt mechanism; after unknown remote effect reconcile rather than blindly recompose.

Adapt the existing JmapClient, not another provider implementation. Bind provider account to the authenticated canonical account namespace, resolve remote thread membership with Thread/get then bounded Email/get, and preserve Mailbox/get, Email/query/get/set, compose, upload/download and subscribe. Read actual submission status through provider capability; perform independent email/submission read-back and record cursor/watch state before claiming observed revision. Subscription is a refresh hint, not durable domain event storage. Preserve loopback-only provisioning and external-recipient restrictions.

After root resolves proposed identifiers, apply one coordinated additive schema/backfill: workspace/entity composite FK, schema_version>0/revision>=0, timestamps/tombstones, account owner/delegated grants, UNIQUE(workspace_id,provider,provider_account_id) and scoped remote aliases, immutable body/blob references, separate token refs and stable inbox cursor indexes. Message-ID is not unique mailbox identity. Use accepted command/outbox/consumer tables instead of redeclaring them; quarantine ambiguous legacy IDs and retain old writer snapshot for pre-cutover rollback.

Exercise exact seven acceptance criteria, strict transport rejection, owner/delegate/outsider and same-address workspace cases, canonical identity/search watermark, provider submission receipt and independent read-back, duplicate/drop/out-of-order event controls and crash between commit/reply. Use seed 20260947 and PRIVATE_WP-17; mocked adapter tests remain explicitly fixture evidence. Runtime Electron/provider scenario evidence must be separate from deterministic package tests.

nextExecutableAction: Root accepts this preflight, commits wave0 and supplies revision-bound WP-04/WP-03/WP-06 typed-interface/migration/scenario receipts. Compare each source hash and re-read changed seams, resolve migrator/provider_connection ownership and hidden completeness gates, then begin the normative mail contracts/repository/JMAP adapter in dependency order. First behavioral implementation slice is authorized canonical GetMailThread/QueryInbox through the existing bridge with same-address account isolation, preserving explicit standalone JMAP. No source implementation is authorized or claimed by this report.
risks: Root-owned uncommitted work may change inspected files. Hash mismatch invalidates the affected seam and requires reinspection; dispatch input revision is not proof of current file bytes.
Global mailbox/service/keychain lookup and broadcast are concrete current cross-context seams, not evidence of an observed live exploit; runtime impact has not been exercised.

JMAP provider primary account ID, email address, RFC Message-ID and canonical entity ID are different identities. Dropping namespace or merging by email/message subject corrupts isolation and mailbox copies.

Legacy global secret migration is dangerous for matching email across workspaces/origins. Ownership and original provider provenance must be verified, with ambiguous bindings quarantined; compatibility cannot be perpetual privileged fallback.

EmailSubmission creation is acceptance, not confirmed recipient delivery. Crash after unknown provider effect cannot be repaired by blind compose retry; read-back capability/reconciliation limitations must remain explicit.
Replacing MAIL_IPC contract without migrating direct MailPanels saveDraft/send/file consumers would leave authority bypasses and false sent UI, even if useMail is updated.
Quiet draft failure currently suppresses UI error; source-preserving cutover still requires durable offline draft/replay rather than labelling current autosave complete.
Provider push is lossy refresh, not a transaction outbox. WP-18 owns extended sync reset/webhook mechanisms, but WP-17 still needs its own durable accepted events and reconnect read-back proof.

Both migration filenames are normative proposed paths; applying competing table definitions or recreating shared provider/receipt tables is incorrect. Root owns migrator and cross-package schema integration.

WP-05/WP-51, mention/notification/agent integration and real provider sandbox are hidden completeness gates beyond WP-17's three declared edges; unresolved gates block featureComplete rather than reducing acceptance.
Logs currently include mailbox address/raw provider errors. New observability must redact content and credentials without hiding actionable error classifications or falsely suppressing failures.
This report proves only inspected source seams and a contribution plan; no feature implementation, runtime regression, provider receipt or dependency acceptance has been verified.
